fund_name: iShares iBoxx $ High Yield Corporate Bond ETF
source_kind_detail: issuer fund-download workbook (SpreadsheetML 2003 XML served as .xls, Content-Disposition filename=iShares-iBoxx--High-Yield-Corporate-Bond-ETF_fund.xls), 'Distributions' worksheet; this is the file behind the product page's Data Download button
fetch_method: python requests GET inside the default sandbox (no sandbox override needed); desktop Chrome User-Agent; Referer https://www.ishares.com/

cross_check.description: Issuer product page HTML; its server-rendered Distributions table (embedded JSON in the DistributionV3 component props and in performance.distributions.table) has 233 rows identical to the workbook on ex-date, record date, payable date and every amount (Decimal comparison).

parsing_notes: Workbook is SpreadsheetML XML; the Disclaimers sheet contains unescaped '&' in URLs so bare ampersands were escaped to '&' before ElementTree parsing (no effect on the Distributions sheet). Distributions sheet: 1 header row + 233 data rows, all cells typed String for dates ('Mon DD, YYYY') and Number for amounts. ex_date/pay_date parsed with format '%b %d, %Y'; amount = 'Total Distribution' as float (6 dp in source). For all 233 rows Total Distribution == Income + ST Cap Gains + LT Cap Gains + Return of Capital exactly; ST/LT cap gains and return of capital are 0 on every row, so amount == Income throughout. All entries are cash per-share USD distributions; the sheet contains no splits and no reinvested/undistributed capital-gain lines. No duplicate ex-dates (no summing needed). Payable date >= ex-date on every row. Source is sorted descending; output ascending. Coverage: first ex-date 2007-05-01 (fund inception 2007-04-04; the issuer lists no April 2007 distribution), last ex-date 2026-09-01. Two rows fall after the requested 2026-07-17 horizon (2026-08-03 and 2026-09-01, the latter payable 2026-09-04) and were retained as issuer-published records. Calendar pattern: no January ex-dates in any year; every December has two ex-dates (early December plus a late-December distribution standing in for January), so 12 per full year; 233 = 9 (May-Dec 2007) + 18*12 (2008-2025) + 8 (Feb-Sep 2026). The ishares.com .ajax download endpoints did not yield a distributions file (see urls_tried), which is why the BlackRock get-fund-document endpoint was used.
